Classical Anatolia.fact: There he found himself faced with further Parthian incursions, who had occupied Syria. Between 40 and 38 BC, the parthians penetrated as far as Caria.

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: Between 40 and 38 BC, the parthians penetrated as far as _____
Classical Anatolia.fact: Between 40 and 38 BC, the parthians penetrated as far as Caria.

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society

Classical Anatolia.fact: However, when Antony himself decided to invade Parthian territory in 33 BC the result was a disaster, although he made two further expeditions into Armenia. Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: In 34 BC Antony and _____ decided to distribute the eastern lands between their children (Donations of Alexandria), precipitating yet another civil war (32–30 BC) and the end of the triumvirate
Classical Anatolia.fact: In 34 BC Antony and Cleopatra decided to distribute the eastern lands between their children (Donations of Alexandria), precipitating yet another civil war (32–30 BC) and the end of the triumvirate.

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: Armenia was granted to _____ and Syria and Cilicia to Ptolemy Philadelphus, while Antony retained Western Anatolia
Classical Anatolia.fact: Armenia was granted to Alexander Helios and Syria and Cilicia to Ptolemy Philadelphus, while Antony retained Western Anatolia.

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: Antony was defeated at the _____ of Actium in 31 BC, and died the following year
Classical Anatolia.fact: Antony was defeated at the Battle of Actium in 31 BC, and died the following year.

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: Of the surviving client kingdoms, _____ was the most prominent but was plagued by internal unrest requiring frequent Roman intervention, sometimes for lack of cooperation
Classical Anatolia.fact: Of the surviving client kingdoms, Cappadocia was the most prominent but was plagued by internal unrest requiring frequent Roman intervention, sometimes for lack of cooperation.

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: At various times it acquired lesser _____ and parts of Cilicia, and was unified with Pontus
Classical Anatolia.fact: Armenia was granted to Alexander Helios and Syria and Cilicia to Ptolemy Philadelphus, while Antony retained Western Anatolia. At various times it acquired lesser Armenia and parts of Cilicia, and was unified with Pontus.

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: In exchange for this redistribution of powers, a long history of civil wars came to an end, replaced by the _____ age (27 BC – 14 AD)
Classical Anatolia.fact: In exchange for this redistribution of powers, a long history of civil wars came to an end, replaced by the Augustan age (27 BC – 14 AD).

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: The endless wars had been devastating for _____
Classical Anatolia.fact: The endless wars had been devastating for Asia Minor.

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: Meanwhile, _____ and Armenia continued as client states
Classical Anatolia.fact: Meanwhile, Cappadocia and Armenia continued as client states. Tiberius (14–37) formed the province of Cappadocia in 17, on the death of the last king, Archelaus (38 BC – 17 AD).

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: Tiberius (14–37) formed the province of _____ in 17, on the death of the last king, Archelaus (38 BC – 17 AD)
Classical Anatolia.fact: Meanwhile, Cappadocia and Armenia continued as client states. Tiberius (14–37) formed the province of Cappadocia in 17, on the death of the last king, Archelaus (38 BC – 17 AD).

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: A truce of sorts was worked out in 1 AD between the Romans and the _____
Classical Anatolia.fact: A truce of sorts was worked out in 1 AD between the Romans and the Parthians.

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: Augustus and his descendants formed the Julio-_____ dynasty (27 BC – 68 AD)
Classical Anatolia.fact: Augustus and his descendants formed the Julio-Claudian dynasty (27 BC – 68 AD).

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: Claudius (41–54) dissolved the _____ league and organised Lycia into a province in 43
Classical Anatolia.fact: Claudius (41–54) dissolved the Lycaean league and organised Lycia into a province in 43.

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: Nero (54–68) organised the remaining eastern portion of the kingdom of _____ into a province, after deposing the last king, Polemon II (38–62)
Classical Anatolia.fact: Nero (54–68) organised the remaining eastern portion of the kingdom of Pontus into a province, after deposing the last king, Polemon II (38–62). Pontus consisted of three districts: Pontus Galaticus in the west, bordering on Galatia which was incorporated into that territory; Pontus Polemoniacus in the centre, so called from its capital Polemonium, from the Iris to Pharnacia, annexed into Bithynia et Pontus; and Pontus Cappadocicus in the east, bordering on Cappadocia (Armenia Minor), was inc...

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: Polemon continued as King of _____ until his death
Classical Anatolia.fact: Polemon continued as King of Cilicia until his death.

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: Armenia continued to be a flashpoint between the Romans and _____
Classical Anatolia.fact: Armenia continued to be a flashpoint between the Romans and Parthians.

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: War erupted again in 36, and again in 58 under _____ (54–68)
Classical Anatolia.fact: War erupted again in 36, and again in 58 under Nero (54–68).

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: After a disastrous battle of _____ in 62
Classical Anatolia.fact: After a disastrous battle of Rhandeia in 62.

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: A compromise was worked out with a _____ on the Armenian throne subject to Roman approval
Classical Anatolia.fact: Armenia continued to be a flashpoint between the Romans and Parthians. A compromise was worked out with a Parthian on the Armenian throne subject to Roman approval.

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: In 72 _____ united all the disparate elements of Cilicia into the Roman province, many of which had remained petty dynasties
Classical Anatolia.fact: In 72 Vespasian united all the disparate elements of Cilicia into the Roman province, many of which had remained petty dynasties. Vespasian also created a new composite province of Lycia et Pamphylia in 72, out of Claudius' province of Lycia and the Pamphylia region of the province of Galatia.

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: Vespasian also created a new composite province of Lycia et _____ in 72, out of Claudius' province of Lycia and the Pamphylia region of the province of Galatia
Classical Anatolia.fact: Vespasian also created a new composite province of Lycia et Pamphylia in 72, out of Claudius' province of Lycia and the Pamphylia region of the province of Galatia.

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: Trajan (98–117) finally achieved provincialisation of the troubled region of _____ in 114, albeit for only four years
Classical Anatolia.fact: Trajan (98–117) finally achieved provincialisation of the troubled region of Armenia in 114, albeit for only four years. Parthia had broken with previous agreements of choosing Armenian kings subject to approval of Rome.

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: War with _____ broke out once again in the 2nd century, generally in Rome's favour
Classical Anatolia.fact: War with Parthia broke out once again in the 2nd century, generally in Rome's favour. Parthia had broken with previous agreements of choosing Armenian kings subject to approval of Rome.

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: Parthia had broken with previous agreements of choosing _____ kings subject to approval of Rome
Classical Anatolia.fact: Parthia had broken with previous agreements of choosing Armenian kings subject to approval of Rome.

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: However, the victory was short-lived, Trajan being forced to withdraw to _____, and dying shortly afterwards in 117 AD
Classical Anatolia.fact: However, the victory was short-lived, Trajan being forced to withdraw to Antioch, and dying shortly afterwards in 117 AD.

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: Trajan's successor, _____ (117–138), decided not to persist with the eastern provinces, and Armenia continued to be a source of conflict in this period
Classical Anatolia.fact: Trajan's successor, Hadrian (117–138), decided not to persist with the eastern provinces, and Armenia continued to be a source of conflict in this period.

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: Marcus Aurelius (161–180) was faced with yet another invasion by _____ on assuming the Imperial office
Classical Anatolia.fact: Marcus Aurelius (161–180) was faced with yet another invasion by Parthia on assuming the Imperial office. The war lasted five years and again the Parthian capital was sacked.

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: The war lasted five years and again the _____ capital was sacked
Classical Anatolia.fact: The war lasted five years and again the Parthian capital was sacked.

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: A new threat was the _____ (165–180), which severely affected Asia
Classical Anatolia.fact: A new threat was the Antonine Plague (165–180), which severely affected Asia.

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: There followed another period of instability, the Year of _____, until Septimius Severus (193–211) became Emperor, initiating the Severan dynasty (193–235)
Classical Anatolia.fact: There followed another period of instability, the Year of Five Emperors, until Septimius Severus (193–211) became Emperor, initiating the Severan dynasty (193–235).

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: In 193, the province of Syria was divided by Severus into two sections, _____ in the north, and Syria Phoenicia in the south
Classical Anatolia.fact: In 193, the province of Syria was divided by Severus into two sections, Syria Coele in the north, and Syria Phoenicia in the south.

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: Armenia and the _____ continued to be a problem in the east, with neither side gaining ground in the long term
Classical Anatolia.fact: Armenia and the Parthians continued to be a problem in the east, with neither side gaining ground in the long term.

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: This time _____ invaded Mesopotamia in 195 AD, sacking Ctesiphon again (197)
Classical Anatolia.fact: There followed another period of instability, the Year of Five Emperors, until Septimius Severus (193–211) became Emperor, initiating the Severan dynasty (193–235). This time Septimius Severus invaded Mesopotamia in 195 AD, sacking Ctesiphon again (197).

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: Caracalla (198–217) had some successes, but these were lost under his successor _____ (217–218)
Classical Anatolia.fact: Caracalla (198–217) had some successes, but these were lost under his successor Macrinus (217–218).

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: However, the _____ itself was about to come to an end, being overthrown in 224 by the resurgent Sasanian Empire, a new threat to the eastern empire
Classical Anatolia.fact: However, the Parthian Empire itself was about to come to an end, being overthrown in 224 by the resurgent Sasanian Empire, a new threat to the eastern empire.

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: Most were either murdered or died in military campaigns against _____'s enemies that were now pressing hard on her frontiers
Classical Anatolia.fact: Most were either murdered or died in military campaigns against Rome's enemies that were now pressing hard on her frontiers.

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: The profound changes between the preceding _____ and succeeding Dominate, coincide with a shift from classical antiquity to late antiquity
Classical Anatolia.fact: The profound changes between the preceding Principate and succeeding Dominate, coincide with a shift from classical antiquity to late antiquity.

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: Persia again attacked in 251, annexing _____ and invading Syria in the reign of Trebonianus Gallus (251–253) but was eventually beaten off by the local Roman forces towards the end of his reign
Classical Anatolia.fact: A Persian invasion starting in 236 in the reign of Gordian III (238–244) prompted Roman retaliation, but in the ensuing battle to secure the eastern borders, the young Gordian was killed, and amongst the terms made was the ceding of Armenia to Persia. Persia again attacked in 251, annexing Armenia and invading Syria in the reign of Trebonianus Gallus (251–253) but was eventually beaten off by the local Roman forces towards the end of his reign.

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: The capture of _____ and Chalcedon by the Goths forced Valerian (253–260) to move his main troop deployments to Cappadocia, weakening his efforts to contain the Sassanid threat
Classical Anatolia.fact: The capture of Nicomedia and Chalcedon by the Goths forced Valerian (253–260) to move his main troop deployments to Cappadocia, weakening his efforts to contain the Sassanid threat.

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: In the course of these latter campaigns, Valerian became the first Roman emperor to be captured by enemy forces, in _____
Classical Anatolia.fact: The capture of Nicomedia and Chalcedon by the Goths forced Valerian (253–260) to move his main troop deployments to Cappadocia, weakening his efforts to contain the Sassanid threat. In the course of these latter campaigns, Valerian became the first Roman emperor to be captured by enemy forces, in 260.

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: The major part of the Roman response fell to the forces in Syrian outpost, _____'s successor, Gallienus (260–268), being preoccupied in the west
Classical Anatolia.fact: The capture of Nicomedia and Chalcedon by the Goths forced Valerian (253–260) to move his main troop deployments to Cappadocia, weakening his efforts to contain the Sassanid threat. In the course of these latter campaigns, Valerian became the first Roman emperor to be captured by enemy forces, in 260.

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: The Sassanid forces penetrated as far west as _____ and Cappadocia
Classical Anatolia.fact: The Sassanid forces penetrated as far west as Isauria and Cappadocia.

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: Asia Minor then experienced the combined attacks of the _____ in the Balkans pouring into Thrace, while their Black Sea relatives ravaged coastal cities
Classical Anatolia.fact: Asia Minor then experienced the combined attacks of the Danubian Goths in the Balkans pouring into Thrace, while their Black Sea relatives ravaged coastal cities.

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: A later emperor, Carus (282–284), led an expedition east to restore Roman rule in _____ and reverse earlier losses by taking on the Sassanids, but died on the campaign
Classical Anatolia.fact: A later emperor, Carus (282–284), led an expedition east to restore Roman rule in Armenia and reverse earlier losses by taking on the Sassanids, but died on the campaign.

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: What ensued was a huge embarrassment for _____- the wealth of the city was absconded, a larger number of ships were confiscated, and they entered the interior without much resistance
Classical Anatolia.fact: Using a captured fleet of ships from the Bosphorus and flat-bottomed boats to cross the Black Sea, they sailed from Black Sea bases (Black Sea Goths) in 255 during the reign of Valerian (253–260) around the eastern shores, landing in the coastal city of Trebizond in Pontus. What ensued was a huge embarrassment for Pontus- the wealth of the city was absconded, a larger number of ships were confiscated, and they entered the interior without much resistance.

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: They entered the city of _____, using it as a base by which to expand their operations, sacking Nicomedia, Prusa, Apamea, and Nicaea in turn
Classical Anatolia.fact: They entered the city of Chalcedon, using it as a base by which to expand their operations, sacking Nicomedia, Prusa, Apamea, and Nicaea in turn.

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: However, the Goths continued their seaborn attacks not only around the coastline of Anatolia, but in _____ and Italy as well
Classical Anatolia.fact: However, the Goths continued their seaborn attacks not only around the coastline of Anatolia, but in Greece and Italy as well.

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: Amongst their raids was the destruction of the Temple of Diana in _____ and the city itself in 263
Classical Anatolia.fact: Amongst their raids was the destruction of the Temple of Diana in Ephesus and the city itself in 263.

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: Tacitus (275–276) successfully took on the _____ invaders of Anatolia, and this was continued by a subsequent emperor, Probus (276–82)
Classical Anatolia.fact: Tacitus (275–276) successfully took on the Gothic invaders of Anatolia, and this was continued by a subsequent emperor, Probus (276–82).

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: In 260 the provinces in the east including Syria broke away to form the _____ (260–273)
Classical Anatolia.fact: In 260 the provinces in the east including Syria broke away to form the Palmyrene Empire (260–273).

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: This stretched all the way to Ancyra, and even attempted to annex _____
Classical Anatolia.fact: This stretched all the way to Ancyra, and even attempted to annex Bithynia.

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: Aurelian (270–275), one of the _____ emperors, was an exception to the general pattern in this era, succeeding in re-uniting the empire by 274
Classical Anatolia.fact: Aurelian (270–275), one of the Illyrian emperors, was an exception to the general pattern in this era, succeeding in re-uniting the empire by 274.

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: By the time of _____, the idea of two empires, west and east was emerging
Classical Anatolia.fact: By the time of Carus, the idea of two empires, west and east was emerging. Carus appointed one of his sons, Carinus (282–285) as co-emperor for the western empire, while he and his other son, Numerian (283–284) concerned themselves with the east.

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: Carus appointed one of his sons, _____ (282–285) as co-emperor for the western empire, while he and his other son, Numerian (283–284) concerned themselves with the east
Classical Anatolia.fact: Carus appointed one of his sons, Carinus (282–285) as co-emperor for the western empire, while he and his other son, Numerian (283–284) concerned themselves with the east. Numerian died before returning west leaving Carinus to face a newly proclaimed emperor, Diocletian, who subsequently triumphed.

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: Numerian died before returning west leaving _____ to face a newly proclaimed emperor, Diocletian, who subsequently triumphed
Classical Anatolia.fact: Carus appointed one of his sons, Carinus (282–285) as co-emperor for the western empire, while he and his other son, Numerian (283–284) concerned themselves with the east. Numerian died before returning west leaving Carinus to face a newly proclaimed emperor, Diocletian, who subsequently triumphed.

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: Diocletian managed to secure the frontiers and instituted sweeping administrative reforms that affected all the provinces, preparing them for the new millennia and the transition to the _____
Classical Anatolia.fact: Diocletian managed to secure the frontiers and instituted sweeping administrative reforms that affected all the provinces, preparing them for the new millennia and the transition to the Early Middle Ages.

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: He continued Carus' tradition by instituting a system of _____, and dividing the responsibility for the empire between them
Classical Anatolia.fact: He continued Carus' tradition by instituting a system of Tetrarchs, and dividing the responsibility for the empire between them.

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: The term _____ became the name of senior emperors, while junior emperors were known as Caesar
Classical Anatolia.fact: The term Augustus became the name of senior emperors, while junior emperors were called Caesar. In the initial arrangement, or Diarchy, Diocletian entrusted the west to his junior Caesar (later Augustus) Maximian while he took charge of the east.

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: In the initial arrangement, or _____, Diocletian entrusted the west to his junior Caesar (later Augustus) Maximian while he took charge of the east
Classical Anatolia.fact: In the initial arrangement, or Diarchy, Diocletian entrusted the west to his junior Caesar (later Augustus) Maximian while he took charge of the east.

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: The new co-emperors were Galerius and Constantius, forming the First Tetrarchy (_____–305)
Classical Anatolia.fact: The new co-emperors were Galerius and Constantius, forming the First Tetrarchy (293–305).

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: Thus Diocletian and _____ were the Augusti (senior emperors) with Galerius and Constantius as Caesares (junior emperors)
Classical Anatolia.fact: In the initial arrangement, or Diarchy, Diocletian entrusted the west to his junior Caesar (later Augustus) Maximian while he took charge of the east. Thus Diocletian and Maximian were the Augusti (senior emperors) with Galerius and Constantius as Caesares (junior emperors).

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: There were now four _____, with the east being governed from Nicomedia in Bithynia (now Izmit), where he had originally been proclaimed emperor
Classical Anatolia.fact: There were now four Tetrarchic Capitals, with the east being governed from Nicomedia in Bithynia (now Izmit), where he had originally been proclaimed emperor.

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: This became the base for defence against invasion from the _____ and Persia's Sassanids and Diocletian's capital
Classical Anatolia.fact: This became the base for defence against invasion from the Balkans and Persia's Sassanids and Diocletian's capital.

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: In the _____ reforms provinces were divided into smaller units, almost doubling the total number soon after 293, replicating the original regions of Asia Minor
Classical Anatolia.fact: Thus Diocletian and Maximian were the Augusti (senior emperors) with Galerius and Constantius as Caesares (junior emperors). This became the base for defence against invasion from the Balkans and Persia's Sassanids and Diocletian's capital.

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: Asia was divided into seven smaller provinces, and _____ three (Bithynia, Honorias and Paphlagonia)
Classical Anatolia.fact: There were now four Tetrarchic Capitals, with the east being governed from Nicomedia in Bithynia (now Izmit), where he had originally been proclaimed emperor. Asia was divided into seven smaller provinces, and Bithynia three (Bithynia, Honorias and Paphlagonia).

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: Galatia lost its northern and southern parts to the new provinces of _____ and Lycaonia, respectively
Classical Anatolia.fact: Asia was divided into seven smaller provinces, and Bithynia three (Bithynia, Honorias and Paphlagonia). Galatia lost its northern and southern parts to the new provinces of Paphlagonia and Lycaonia, respectively.

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: Lycia et _____ was once again split into its two constituent units
Classical Anatolia.fact: Lycia et Pamphylia was once again split into its two constituent units.

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: Cappadocia lost its _____ and Lesser Armenian territories
Classical Anatolia.fact: Cappadocia lost its Pontic and Lesser Armenian territories. Anatolia was restructured into three dioceses, which were eventually grouped under the Praetorian Prefecture of the East (praefectura praetorio Orientis); Asia (Asiana), Pontus (Pontica) and East (Oriens).

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: Anatolia was restructured into three dioceses, which were eventually grouped under the _____ of the East (praefectura praetorio Orientis); Asia (Asiana), Pontus (Pontica) and East (Oriens)
Classical Anatolia.fact: Anatolia was restructured into three dioceses, which were eventually grouped under the Praetorian Prefecture of the East (praefectura praetorio Orientis); Asia (Asiana), Pontus (Pontica) and East (Oriens).

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: (see navbox below) _____ returned to the Roman sphere in 287 as a vassal state under Tiridates III (287–330) and more formally as protectorate in 299
Classical Anatolia.fact: Cappadocia lost its Pontic and Lesser Armenian territories. (see navbox below) Armenia returned to the Roman sphere in 287 as a vassal state under Tiridates III (287–330) and more formally as protectorate in 299.

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: Galerius was now _____ of the East and the Second Tetrarchy was formed with Constantius and Galerius as Augusti and Severus and Maximinus as Caesares, and heirs apparent
Classical Anatolia.fact: This happened but the expected new Caesares were not, as expected, the sons of former emperors, Maxentius (son of the now retired Augustus Maximian) and Constantine (son of the new Augustus Constantius), but rather Flavius Valerius Severus and Maximinus. Galerius was now Augustus of the East and the Second Tetrarchy was formed with Constantius and Galerius as Augusti and Severus and Maximinus as Caesares, and heirs apparent.

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: This oversight was to prove fatal to _____'s vision of a tetrarchy
Classical Anatolia.fact: On the eastern front, Persia renewed hostilities in 296, inflicting losses on Galerius' forces, until Diocletian brought in new troops from further west the following year and clashed with the Persians in lesser Armenia, and pursued them all the way to Ctesiphon in 298, effectively ending the campaign. This oversight was to prove fatal to Diocletian's vision of a tetrarchy.

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: Constantius died in 306 and _____ raised Severus to Augustus as expected
Classical Anatolia.fact: Galerius was now Augustus of the East and the Second Tetrarchy was formed with Constantius and Galerius as Augusti and Severus and Maximinus as Caesares, and heirs apparent. Constantius died in 306 and Galerius raised Severus to Augustus as expected.

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: This left multiple candidates for the _____ roles
Classical Anatolia.fact: This left multiple candidates for the Tetrarchical roles.

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: The transition from _____ to Galerius proceeded smoothly in 305
Classical Anatolia.fact: The transition from Diocletian to Galerius proceeded smoothly in 305.

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: Upon assuming the role of _____, Galerius assigned Maximinus to Egypt and Syria
Classical Anatolia.fact: Upon assuming the role of Augustus, Galerius assigned Maximinus to Egypt and Syria. On Galerius'death in 311, Maximinus divided the east seizing Asia Minor, with Licinius as western Augustus.

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: Constantine had disposed of _____ in 312 and agreed to repartition the empire, with Constantine in the west and Licinius in the East
Classical Anatolia.fact: Constantine had disposed of Maxentius in 312 and agreed to repartition the empire, with Constantine in the west and Licinius in the East.

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: Licinius was immediately engaged in dealing with the _____ situation
Classical Anatolia.fact: Licinius was immediately engaged in dealing with the Persian situation.

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: Constantine eventually besieged _____ in Byzantium in 324, defeated his fleet at the Battle of Hellespont
Classical Anatolia.fact: Constantine had disposed of Maxentius in 312 and agreed to repartition the empire, with Constantine in the west and Licinius in the East. Licinius was immediately engaged in dealing with the Persian situation.

Classical Anatolia.subject: Indian Society
Classical Anatolia.question: Licinius fell back on _____, where he surrendered at the Battle of Chrysopolis
